newsitem.title: USA: Aviron rises on strong flu vaccine data.
newsitem.headline: Aviron rises on strong flu vaccine data.

text.p: Shares of Aviron rose sharply Tuesday, boosted by surprisingly strong data on the nasal spray flu vaccine it is developing, analysts said.

The company reported that only one percent of children given the vaccine in a trial developed influenza, compared with 18 percent of those who were given a placebo. No adverse side effects were reported.

Analysts said they expect the strong trial data will not only help Aviron win Food and Drug Administration approval for the vaccine, but secure a larger share of the market than had earlier been anticipated. Aviron is aiming to have the vaccine approved for children in time for the 1999-2000 flu season.

"The data was so strong and so unequivocably positive that I think (market) penetration will be stronger than we'd assumed," said Robertson Stephens analyst Jay Silverman, who raised his 12-month target price on the stock to $31 per share. In May, Silverman had issued a 12-month target price of $24.

"We'd been assuming that the vaccine would be given to four to five percent of all children in the U.S. within five years of the time it was approved," Silverman added. "With these trial results, it could be 10 percent."

He also said the strong trial data would help the company penetrate the adult and elderly population flu vaccine market. It currently has separate trials underway testing the vaccine in those populations.

Aviron was not immediately avaiable for comment on Tuesday, but has said in the past that it may be able to seek approval of the vaccine for adults without producing separate trial data if the children's trial data were compelling.
The Aviron flu vaccine can be self-administered with a spray in each nostril.
